name: Scales & Borders
description: Symmetric repeating linear gradient borders and geometric scale dividers.
summary: Technical boundary elements and scale dividers that replace generic horizontal rules with an architectural, developer-console look. Built with CSS repeating linear gradients (315deg, a 1px line every 10px inside 14px x 14px tiles) and theme CSS custom properties (--pattern-line, --pattern), with no JavaScript runtime.
highlights: Pure CSS repeating-linear-gradient shader rendering with zero JavaScript overhead
Zero cumulative layout shift (CLS 0.0) with GPU-accelerated compositing
Three specialized geometric layout variants: HorizontalScale, VerticalScale, and Lines
Themeable token variables (--pattern-line, --pattern) for seamless light/dark adaptation
14px background tile with a 1px line repeating every 10px
anatomy: <HorizontalScale> (40px horizontal ribbon with diagonal 315° repeating hatch marks)
<VerticalScale> (40px vertical divider with diagonal 315° repeating hatch marks)
<Lines> (56px horizontal scanline guide with high-density repeating lines)

physics.description: Zero-runtime GPU rasterized gradient stripes calculated via repeating linear-gradient geometry without layout repaints.

accessibility.aria: Renders an empty div with no role or ARIA attributes. Only className is accepted, so wrap it in an element with role="separator" or aria-hidden="true" if needed.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Static CSS background gradient pattern; completely unaffected by motion preferences.

recommended: Technical panel dividers in developer tools, IDE views, and engineering dashboards
Header and footer section breaks in technical documentation sites
Visual framing boundaries around code editors, telemetry viewers, and terminal displays
bestPractices: Define --pattern-line and --pattern in your theme root for consistent contrast across light and dark modes
Use VerticalScale inside flex containers with h-full for crisp column separation
Override the default h-10 / h-14 height or w-10 width with className
